title: Beginner Pack 1
subtitle: Practice in context · Preview
label: 3 patterns · 6 questions
description: Use familiar Level 1 kanji and vocabulary in short everyday sentences across three foundational grammar patterns.

patterns.readingNote: は is pronounced “wa” when used as the topic particle.
patterns.summary: は marks the topic you are talking about (A), and です politely states what that topic is (B).

examples.japanese: ふじ山は大きい山です。
examples.reading: ふじさんは おおきい やま です。
examples.gloss: ふじ山 Mt. Fuji · 大きい big · 山 mountain
examples.english: Mt. Fuji is a big mountain.

examples.reading: あの ひとは おとな です。
examples.gloss: あの人 that person · 大人 adult

questions.japanese: ふじ山は大きい山です。
questions.reading: ふじさんは おおきい やま です。
questions.gloss: ふじ山 Mt. Fuji · 大きい big · 山 mountain

choices.text: Mt. Fuji is above the mountain.
choices.explanation: Not quite. 大きい (おおきい) means “big,” not “above” (上, うえ). In ふじ山は大きい山です, 大きい modifies 山 (“a big mountain”).

choices.text: Mt. Fuji is a big mountain.
choices.explanation: That’s right! ふじ山は sets Mt. Fuji as the topic (A), and 大きい山です states what it is (B: “is a big mountain”).

choices.text: There is a big person on Mt. Fuji.
choices.explanation: Not quite. 大きい山 means “big mountain” (山), not “adult / big person” (大人), and です means “is,” not “there is a person” (います).

followUp.prompt: Follow-up check — What does this new sentence mean?
followUp.japanese: あの女の人は大人です。
followUp.reading: あの おんなの ひとは おとな です。
followUp.gloss: あの女の人 that woman · 大人 adult

choices.explanation: That’s right! あの女の人は sets “that woman” as the topic (A), and 大人です states what she is (B: “is an adult”).
Not quite. A は B です states that A is B; it does not mean “has” or “two people” (二人).

choices.text: That person is a big mountain.
choices.explanation: Not quite. 大人 (おとな) means “adult” (not 大きい山, “big mountain”), and あの女の人 means “that woman.”

workedExample.japanese: あの女の人は大人です。
workedExample.reading: あの おんなの ひとは おとな です。
workedExample.breakdown: Step 1: あの女の人 (“that woman”) + は marks the topic you are talking about (A). Step 2: 大人 (“adult”) + です politely states what that topic is (B). Together: “That woman is an adult.”

questions.prompt: Choose the particle that marks “this (これ)” as the topic of the sentence:
questions.japanese: これ（　）ビルの入り口です。
questions.reading: これ（　）ビルの いりぐち です。
questions.gloss: これ this · ビル building · 入り口 entrance

choices.explanation: Not quite. を marks the direct object of an action verb, so it cannot pair with the copula です in an “A is B” sentence.
Not quite. に marks a location, time, or destination, not the topic of an “A is B” (…です) sentence.
That’s right! は marks これ (“this”) as the topic of the A は B です identification sentence (“This is the building’s entrance”).

followUp.prompt: Follow-up check — Choose the particle that marks “that mountain (あの山)” as the topic:
followUp.reading: あの やま（　）ふじさん です。
followUp.gloss: あの山 that mountain · ふじ山 Mt. Fuji

choices.explanation: Not quite. を marks the object of an action verb, whereas です needs a topic marked by は.
That’s right! は marks あの山 (“that mountain”) as the topic (A) before ふじ山です (B: “is Mt. Fuji”).
Not quite. に marks where something exists or goes, not the topic of ふじ山です.

workedExample.reading: あの やまは ふじさん です。
workedExample.breakdown: Step 1: Identify who or what the sentence is about: あの山 (“that mountain”). Step 2: Place は right after the topic (あの山は). Step 3: State what it is with ふじ山です (“is Mt. Fuji”).

patterns.readingNote: In A の B, the main noun being talked about always comes second (B).
patterns.summary: の connects two nouns so the first noun (A) describes or narrows down the second noun (B).

examples.japanese: ここは駅の入り口です。
examples.reading: ここは えきの いりぐち です。
examples.gloss: ここ here · 駅 station · 入り口 entrance
examples.english: Here is the entrance to the station.

examples.japanese: 日本の山はきれいです。
examples.reading: にほんの やまは きれいです。
examples.gloss: 日本 Japan · 山 mountain · きれい beautiful

questions.prompt: Choose the particle that links 駅 (station) to 入り口 (entrance) to mean “the entrance to the station”:
questions.targetMeaning: Here is the entrance to the station.
questions.reading: ここは えき（　）いりぐち です。
questions.gloss: ここ here · 駅 station · 入り口 entrance

choices.explanation: That’s right! の connects the two nouns (駅 + 入り口) so 駅 modifies 入り口 (“the entrance to the station”).
Not quite. Putting は after 駅 creates an ungrammatical double-topic after ここは (“As for here, the station is an entrance”) instead of linking the two nouns with の.
Not quite. を marks the direct object of a transitive action verb, so it cannot connect two nouns before です.

followUp.prompt: Follow-up check — Choose the particle that links ホテル (hotel) to 入り口 (entrance) to mean “the entrance to the hotel”:
followUp.japanese: これはホテル（　）入り口です。
followUp.targetMeaning: This is the entrance to the hotel.
followUp.reading: これは ホテル（　）いりぐち です。
followUp.gloss: これ this · ホテル hotel · 入り口 entrance

choices.explanation: Not quite. これ is already marked as the topic with は; connecting the two nouns ホテル and 入り口 requires の.
Not quite. を marks the object of a verb, not a noun modifying another noun.
That’s right! の links ホテル (A) to 入り口 (B) to form ホテルの入り口 (“the entrance to the hotel”).

workedExample.japanese: これはホテルの入り口です。
workedExample.reading: これは ホテルの いりぐち です。
workedExample.english: This is the entrance to the hotel.
workedExample.breakdown: Step 1: ホテル (“hotel”) narrows down which 入り口 (“entrance”) we mean. Step 2: Join the describing noun (A: ホテル) to the main noun (B: 入り口) with の → ホテルの入り口 (“the hotel’s entrance”).

questions.gloss: テーブル table · 下 under / below

choices.explanation: Not quite. “Above / on” is 上 (うえ), whereas 下 (した) means “under / below.”

choices.text: a table that is under something
choices.explanation: Not quite. That reverses the A の B order. In テーブルの下, the second noun 下 (“the area under”) is the main noun and テーブル tells you what it is under.
That’s right! In A の B, the second noun 下 (“under / area below”) is the head noun, and テーブル specifies what it belongs to: “under the table.”

followUp.prompt: Follow-up check — What does this phrase mean?
followUp.gloss: 机 desk · 上 on / above

choices.text: a desk that is above something
choices.explanation: Not quite. That reverses the A の B word order: the second noun 上 (“top / area above”) is the head noun, modified by 机 (“desk”).
That’s right! In 机の上, the second noun 上 (“top / area above”) is the head noun and 机 (“desk”) specifies what it belongs to: “on / above the desk.”
Not quite. “Under” is 下 (した), whereas 上 (うえ) means “on / above.”

workedExample.breakdown: Step 1: In A の B, the second noun (B) is always the main thing: 上 (うえ, “the top / space above”). Step 2: The first noun (A) tells you what it belongs to: 机 (つくえ, “desk”). Together: “the top of the desk” (“on / above the desk”).

patterns.pattern: A に B が あります
patterns.gloss: There is B in/at/on A (non-living things)
patterns.readingNote: あります is used for non-living things; living people and animals use います.
patterns.summary: Use Location に + Thing が あります to say that a non-living thing (B) exists at a place (A). Quantity counters like 二つ or 三つ can go right before あります.

examples.japanese: このビルに入り口が二つあります。
examples.reading: この ビルに いりぐちが ふたつ あります。
examples.gloss: このビル this building · 入り口 entrance · 二つ two things
examples.english: There are two entrances in this building.

examples.reading: へやに つくえが あります。
examples.english: There is a desk in the room.

questions.prompt: Choose the word that completes “There are two entrances in this building”:
questions.japanese: このビルに入り口が二つ（　）。
questions.targetMeaning: There are two entrances in this building.
questions.reading: この ビルに いりぐちが ふたつ（　）。
questions.gloss: このビル this building · 入り口 entrance · 二つ two things

choices.explanation: Not quite. います is only for living, animate beings (people and animals), whereas 入り口 (entrances) are non-living things.
That’s right! あります expresses the existence of non-living things like 入り口 (“There are two entrances in this building”).
Not quite. 入ります (はいります) is the verb “to enter.” Although it shares the kanji 入 with 入り口, here it would mean “two entrances enter the building.”

followUp.prompt: Follow-up check — Choose the word that completes “There is one big desk in the room”:
followUp.japanese: へやに大きい机が一つ（　）。
followUp.targetMeaning: There is one big desk in the room.
followUp.reading: へやに おおきい つくえが ひとつ（　）。
followUp.gloss: へや room · 大きい big · 机 desk · 一つ one thing

choices.explanation: Not quite. います is reserved for living beings (people and animals), whereas a desk (机) is non-living.
Not quite. 上げます (あげます) means “to raise / lift something,” not “there is.”
That’s right! Because a desk (机) is a non-living thing, あります completes “There is one big desk in the room.”

workedExample.japanese: へやに大きい机が一つあります。
workedExample.reading: へやに おおきい つくえが ひとつ あります。
workedExample.english: There is one big desk in the room.
workedExample.breakdown: Step 1: へやに marks the location (“in the room”). Step 2: 大きい机が一つ names the non-living object and count (“one big desk”). Step 3: Use あります (never います) for non-living things.

questions.japanese: テーブルの上にりんごが三つあります。
questions.reading: テーブルの うえに りんごが みっつ あります。
questions.gloss: テーブル table · 上 on / above · りんご apple · 三つ three things

choices.text: There are three apples on the table.
choices.explanation: That’s right! テーブルの上に marks the location (“on the table”), りんごが三つ names the item and counter (“three apples”), and あります states they are there.

choices.text: There are three people at the table.
choices.explanation: Not quite. 三つ (みっつ) counts inanimate things (paired with あります), whereas three people would be 三人 (さんにん) with います.

choices.text: There are three apples under the table.
choices.explanation: Not quite. 上 (うえ) means “on / above,” not 下 (した, “under”). In テーブルの上にりんごが三つあります, the three apples are on top of the table.

followUp.prompt: Follow-up check — What does this new sentence mean?
followUp.japanese: 机の下に箱が二つあります。
followUp.reading: つくえの したに はこが ふたつ あります。
followUp.gloss: 机 desk · 下 under / below · 箱 box · 二つ two things

choices.text: There are two boxes under the desk.
choices.explanation: That’s right! 机の下に marks the location (“under the desk”), 箱が二つ names the object and counter (“two boxes”), and あります states they exist there.

choices.text: There are two people under the desk.
choices.explanation: Not quite. 箱が二つ with あります counts non-living boxes (“two boxes”), whereas two people would be 二人 (ふたり) with います.

choices.text: There are three boxes on the desk.
choices.explanation: Not quite. 下 (した) means “under” (not 上, “on”), and 二つ (ふたつ) means “two things” (not 三つ, “three things”).

workedExample.japanese: 机の下に箱が二つあります。
workedExample.reading: つくえの したに はこが ふたつ あります。
workedExample.english: There are two boxes under the desk.
workedExample.breakdown: Step 1: 机の下に = “under the desk” (location + に). Step 2: 箱が二つ = “two boxes” (non-living noun + が + counter 二つ). Step 3: あります = “there are” (for inanimate things).

sources: Komorebi Level 1 curriculum (data/level-1.json): kanji 山, 大, 人, 入, 口, 上, 下, 二, 三 and vocabulary ふじ山, 大きい, 山, 人, 大人, 入り口, 上, 下, 二つ, 三つ, 入る, 三人.
JLPT N5 foundational grammar progression: A は B です (topic + copula), A の B (noun modification, cf. Renshuu #109), and A に B が あります (inanimate existence, cf. Renshuu #108).
All example sentences, fresh transfer prompts, follow-up questions, worked examples, brief glosses, and distractor explanations are original reviewed study material authored for Komorebi.
